**Finding: compliant** (preferred position) — no redline proposed.

**What I checked and found:**

- **No exclusivity binding us.** Every "exclusive" reference in the document is either neutral or runs in our favour as a scope limit on the licence itself: the grant is a "non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use" (p0030), echoed in the Preamble, term (p0049) and fee provisions (p0052). Licensor also reserves the right to license to others (p0043) — so exclusivity is neither granted to us nor demanded of us.
- **No requirements or sole-sourcing covenant.** Searches for "sole", "shall not use any other", "all transactions", and "third party" surfaced no commitment to buy all requirements from Licensor, no covenant against procuring competing FX technology, and no obligation to route volume solely through the Platform.
- **The planner's ROFR lead did not bear out.** Article XXII (p0139) is a change-of-control/exit right — a five-business-day right to match a bona fide third-party offer to buy Licensee's assets or merge with Licensee — not a foreclosure of alternative suppliers. It expressly releases us to close with the third party if Licensor declines or fails to exercise (p0140–p0141).
- **Article II restrictions are licence-scope, not exclusive dealing.** p0027, p0041 and p0044 restrict resale, sublicensing and derivative works of *Licensor's own* technology — standard IP protection, not restrictive covenants on our procurement freedom.

**Noted in the rationale, not flagged:** the ROFR and the Change of Control provision (p0134) do constrain our exit flexibility. That is a separate commercial issue properly assessed under the assignment/change-of-control rule, so I deliberately did not flag it here to avoid double-flagging the same term under two rules.
